high.title: Gold ring prices, gold bar prices morning 20/5
high.summary: International gold prices recorded at $4,481/ounce at the start of the morning session, up slightly 0.01% from the previous close, after falling over 1.8% in the previous trading session. Gold prices fell sharply due to pressure from a strengthening USD and persistent inflation concerns, causing markets to increase expectations that interest rates will remain high for an extended period. The strengthening USD and rising US 10-year Treasury yields near their highest level in over a year are creating unfavorable conditions for the precious metal. Rising bond yields increase the opportunity cost of holding gold - a non-yielding asset - making it less attractive to investors. This development has direct implications for Vietnamese gold markets and could influence SBV's foreign reserve management strategy.

high.title: Gold ring prices, gold bar prices morning 21/5
high.summary: International gold prices opened at $4,538/ounce, down 0.1% from the previous close, after gaining nearly 1.4% in the previous session. Gold rebounded when expectations of de-escalation in Iran conflict helped reduce pressure on oil markets, easing inflation concerns and pulling US bond yields away from recent peaks. The 10-year US Treasury yield declined slightly after touching its highest level since January 2025. Lower yields reduce pressure on gold by decreasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets. Any positive signals regarding conflict resolution could further support gold prices by reducing geopolitical risk premiums and potentially influencing central bank reserve allocations including Vietnam's foreign reserves.

high.title: Securities firms comment on VN-Index's sudden reversal session
high.summary: Vietnam's stock market continues trading near the historic high of 1,900 points on the VN-Index, but stronger volatility is emerging as money flows rapidly rotate between stock groups. On May 20, selling pressure occurred broadly, causing the index to drop to 1,860 points at one point, but buying support at lower levels helped VN-Index recover and even close slightly positive. Dragon Capital Securities (VDSC) noted the market recorded a cautious correction session when VN-Index negated previous gains and closed at 1,912.93 points. The deep decline of up to 50 points showed market support efforts were not clear and red dominated the session. This volatility at historic highs signals potential distribution phase and requires close monitoring for FX and equity traders.

high.title: Did sell-off investors "lose shares" after VN-Index's 50+ point reversal?
high.summary: After VN-Index's "roller coaster" session losing over 50 points then sharply recovering at session end, many investors wonder whether large money flows are returning to "accumulate" or bull trap risks remain. According to Luong Duy Phuoc, Research Director at Kafi Securities, the "roller coaster" movement reflects very strong market tug-of-war after a rapid rise period heavily dependent on large-cap stocks. When blue-chip stocks faced profit-taking pressure, selling quickly spread to other sectors, especially stocks that had heated up recently. However, the strong late-session recovery showed buying power at low prices was waiting to participate, proving the market hasn't fallen into uncontrolled sell-off status. This technical action at 1,900 levels is critical for assessing whether Vietnam's equity market can sustain current valuations.

medium.title: One bank offers 8.5%/year interest rate for deposits from 500,000 VND
medium.summary: VietBank launched a promotional program offering up to 8.5%/year interest rates for new savings accounts, with 6-11 month terms at 8.3%/year, 12-14 month terms at 8.4%/year, and 15-month terms at 8.5%/year. This aggressive deposit rate strategy reflects ongoing competition in Vietnam's banking sector and potential liquidity pressures.

medium.title: "Big player" Agribank closes multiple transaction offices, reorganizes entire network
medium.summary: Agribank announced comprehensive network restructuring at Nam Dinh branch, closing multiple transaction offices while reorganizing operations for efficiency. The move aligns with Resolution 18-NQ/TW on streamlining organizational apparatus and reflects broader banking sector consolidation trends that could impact regional credit flows.

medium.title: Banks lend and borrow trillions of VND from each other: Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV and Agribank are the largest creditors
medium.summary: As of end-March 2026, Vietcombank had net lending position of 214.337 trillion VND in interbank market, followed by VietinBank (138.361 trillion) and BIDV (91.471 trillion). The three state banks created total net lending of ~444,000 trillion VND, highlighting their central role in liquidity distribution and potential SBV monetary policy transmission mechanisms.

medium.title: One bank few think about has bad debt ratio nearly lowest in system, lower than ACB, Techcombank, VietinBank
medium.summary: ABBank surprised with NPL ratio of just 0.82%, dramatically improved from 3.8% a year ago. The five lowest NPL ratios are: Vietcombank (0.62%), ABBank (0.82%), ACB (0.97%), VietinBank (1.02%) and Techcombank (1.09%). This reflects improving asset quality trends in Vietnam's banking sector.

medium.title: An MB Bank Deputy CEO registers to sell large volume of MBB shares
medium.summary: MB Bank Deputy CEO Pham Thi Trung Ha registered to sell 1 million MBB shares (estimated 25 billion VND at current prices) for personal financial needs, reducing her stake from 0.0501% to 0.0377%. This insider selling activity should be monitored for potential market sentiment impacts.
